speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: As such, can MINDEF share on how we can best ensure our announced F-35 purchases will be cost-effective, while delivering the required capabilities to keep Singapore secure?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The use of this has become integrated into many aspects of defence.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: On the other hand, cyberattacks and breaches are also getting more innovative, threatening, complex and widespread.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Cyber threats do not fit into traditional security framework.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: So, therefore, Singapore cannot let down our guard.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: We are on the radar and the target of many, due to a variety of factors.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It will help in training officers in preparedness, thinking several steps ahead of the perpetrator and culprits.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How is MINDEF upscaling cyber defence and security and ringfencing, with a view to fortifying our national and defence cybersecurity systems?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: In alignment with this, can the Ministry also update us on what further efforts are being pursued to continue to develop the area of cyber defence and expertise in the SAF?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can we also have an update on the Cyber NS Scheme and how MINDEF intends to boost our cyber defence expertise in the military?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Knowing also that the military response must be part of a concerted national effort, how is MINDEF's approach coordinated with that of other Ministries and agencies in our national cybersecurity ecosystem?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Chairman, the establishment of Cyber Defence training is key to a future-ready 21st century defence capability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: And these skills will come in useful, not just in the SAF, because the cyber frontline is everywhere anywhere where there is a network, a digital device, a gadget connected to the Internet of Things.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: And so, as successive generations of cyber defence vocationalist graduates complete their full-time NS and become operationally-ready NSmen, these servicemen can add to the pool of cyber defence knowledge and cyber defence instincts in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Can MINDEF share more on how our Cyber Defenders' skills can be accredited and recognised, in ways that will help potential employers, in turn, recognise their value to organisations, workplaces and to Singapore?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Preventing sophisticated cyberattacks by malicious parties is now a critical mission for both governments and companies globally.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Yet, nearly every country in the world lacks cybersecurity talent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Could MINDEF provide an update of the Cyber NSF Scheme?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How will we ensure that our NSFs' expertise is constantly updated and deepened?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We must also collaborate with the private sector to keep up with evolving technologies and be updated to the ceaseless cyber threats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The continual development of cyber defence expertise must go beyond just having the Cyber NSF Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We must also continue to develop them when they reach the Operationally Ready Date (ORD).

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: What are MINDEF's plans to build a strong reservist corp of Cyber NSmen?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In fact, I encourage MINDEF to consider developing a Cyber NSmen Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There are already many NSmen in the IT industry with deep cybersecurity expertise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Some of them are highly-skilled operators while others are already IT industry captains.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Our Cyber NSFs can form the foundation of this Cyber NSmen Scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The Israeli Defence Forces' Unit 8200 has reportedly had many of its servicemen gone on to build many top IT companies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Similarly, our Cyber NSFs can go on to have such impact and help to build up the tech expertise in the private sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We need to ensure that we enrich our Cyber NSFs training, such as providing for a stronger nexus with the startup sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: With this, we can build up dynamic and sustainable cyber capabilities that will protect Singapore at all times.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: We will need to continue to boost our capacity and capabilities and build up our defence capabilities, systems, operations, manpower and technology.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: We need to ensure we maintain our edge at all times.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: This requires state-of-the art mindset, equipment and systems.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: With that background, what will be the projected medium- to longer-term increments in defence spending?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: How are we to balance this against the needs in other competing areas?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: Training also, Sir, requires planning and preparation, more so in terms of teams training, table-top exercises and simulated exercises.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: How will MINDEF be allocating funds into these aspects of development and training as well?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Their sacrifices and their families' sacrifices have kept our country safe and secure.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: NS has served as the backbone of the SAF.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It has been the bedrock of peace for Singapore over the last 50 years.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Even though the probability of conventional conflict is low, I am heartened that the majority of us acknowledge the importance of NS as a deterrent against potential adversaries.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Over the years, our NSmen have responded with distinction to challenges, such as international piracy, terrorism and even natural disasters abroad while, at the same time, deterring potential aggressors.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In today's constantly changing geopolitical environment and in view of the evolving security landscape and threats that are changing rapidly, MINDEF needs to redefine NS.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: At the same time, SAF also needs to respond to the domestic challenge of falling birth rates which requires a paradigm shift in our approach to NS.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Could MINDEF share how it will respond to these challenges and the future warfare and elaborate on the role that NS plays today and its importance to Singapore?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, an ageing population and declining fertility trends will have implications on our NS resources and will pose a significant challenge for us in the long term.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Therefore, there is a clear impetus to effectively manage our NS manpower resource to ensure that MINDEF and SAF are able to achieve its growing spectrum of missions even as the enlistment cohorts decline.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Over the years, MINDEF/SAF has introduced initiatives to allow the SAF to tap on our servicemen's civilian expertise and talent to expand operational capabilities.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How is MINDEF harnessing the expertise of our current pool of servicemen to maximise the potential of our NSmen?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With growing manpower limitations, what is MINDEF/SAF doing to ensure that we can maximise our manpower resources?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will MINDEF consider options taken by other manpower-scarce countries, such as tapping on woman power?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the Ministry consider pushing back or doing away with the retirement age of regulars?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will MINDEF also consider redesigning functions so that in suitable areas, persons with disabilities can also contribute to our national defence?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NS was and continues to be essential for the defence of our nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Fifty-two years on, our country has benefited from relative peace and stability, achieved by a strong SAF that protects Singapore's interests, and supported by generations of NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Recent tensions with our neighbour over sea and air boundaries are a reminder of why we need a credible SAF, one that conducts realistic military training so that our soldiers are operationally-ready.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NS has fulfilled a critical need for defence and security and also provided the peace and stability facilitating Singapore's development and progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Arguably, few national policies affect the Singaporean way of life to the extent that NS does.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For many Singaporean men, NS is a rite of passage, where he takes on the commitment of defending his country at a young age of 18 and, regardless of social standing, race or religion, to be trained and to serve with one another as a unit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I would like MINDEF to provide an update on its efforts to maximise the potential of NSmen and how we can enhance their NS experience.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: NS exists to fulfil the critical need of national security and defence.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: In today's rapidly evolving learning environment, we need to ensure that our NSFs are well-equipped to thrive in higher education or in the working world.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Mr Chairman, earlier this month, the Minister for Defence made a Ministerial Statement on NS training deaths and safety enhancements for the SAF.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The Ministerial Statement addressed some of the circumstances around the untimely death of Corporal First Class (CFC) Aloysius Pang and the Minister also shared some of the findings of the Committee of Inquiry which was convened after CFC Liu Kai was killed in a training accident in November 2018.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The issue of training safety is one which concerns us all.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Every Singaporean family has a family member who has gone through or will go through NS.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: We also have a large number of men and women who have chosen to protect our country as their careers.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Some spend decades in our armed forces, ready to put their lives on the line for Singapore should the need arise.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I am aware that the issue of training safety is not confined just to NSFs but also to the regulars who serve in SAF.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: But this bond of trust we have with the families of NSFs and NSmen, those who are required by law to serve, is where it can be felt most keenly.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: That is not to say that we should mollycoddle our servicemen or that we eliminate activities which carry the slightest amount of risks.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: That is not how a military should be run.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: I would, therefore, like to ask the Minister how do MINDEF and SAF strike a balance between the need for an operationally-ready SAF that is able to defend Singapore's sovereignty with the need to ensure the safety of our soldiers, especially during training.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: We have heard on various occasions that this balance will be struck by MINDEF and SAF and I would like to ask the Minister for clarification as to how this balance is achieved.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: As I mentioned earlier, the first Inspector-General of SAF has just started in his role yesterday.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The appointment of the Inspector-General is a positive step as I understand that there was previously no organisation which covered safety across all branches of SAF.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: The appointment has a strong signalling effect and indicates to our troops how important safety is to our armed forces.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: It was reported that the new Inspector-General stressed the importance of open reporting and that he wants to introduce concrete actions to promote open reporting.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Indeed, the concept of open reporting in safety matters is counter-intuitive.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: In other organisations and industries, the reporting of safety issues and lapses is encouraged through confidential reporting where the identities of those doing the reports are protected.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: This is particularly so if it involves unsafe practices by their superiors and colleagues.

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Are we essentially asking for whistleblowers to come forward with the reports in the open?

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Could the Minister clarify why open reporting would be more successful than confidential reporting?

speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
text: Apart from the appointment of the Inspector-General, I would be grateful if MINDEF could elaborate on other systems and safeguards that they have or will put in place to ensure training safety in SAF, particularly in the light of recent training deaths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, safety is one of the SAF's core values and it is integral to mission success.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It enhances the soldier's confidence and enables the SAF to conduct reality training and to operate effectively during missions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Safety, while an individual responsibility, is also a command responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I understand that our commanders are trained in command schools on the requirements on how to conduct training safely; and safety education and training are also constantly reinforced in the various courses that our commanders go through as they progress in their career.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: During training, I also understand that commanders are responsible for planning a proper work-rest cycle to ensure that their soldiers have sufficient rest, and exercise right judgement to moderate training intensity according to ground conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Despite all the measures that have been put in place, there have been one too many cases of training safety incidents recently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: What is MINDEF doing to ensure that there is command emphasis on training safety on the ground and that it is consistently applied for all the units of SAF so that it can work towards zero training accidents?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui, you have half a minute.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Chairman, since NS was introduced more than five decades ago, generations of Singaporeans had served in various capacities and contributed to our national defence.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The commitment of Singaporeans to serve in peace time allows us to build and maintain a strong armed forces.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Will the Ministry consider building a small memorial there or somewhere else to honour our fallen servicemen?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Chairman, as a member of the MINDEF Advisory Council on Communal Relations (MINDEF ACCORD) for the past three years, I have witnessed first-hand how MINDEF successfully build broad support from society, from businesses, schools and various communities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In particular, I would like to commend MINDEF on its successful engagement of Singaporeans through NS50 in the past year.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: As such, what are MINDEF's plans in the year ahead to engage the community and grassroots leaders to understand and support the importance of NS, as well as our broadened concept of Total Defence?

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Recent events, and the threat of military escalation, have reminded many Singaporeans of the threats surrounding us.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is at times like this, that Singaporeans must understand the threats that we face, and the importance of total defence.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Climate change is resulting in more extreme weather conditions, while state actors and terrorists have shown that they are more than willing to exploit our vulnerabilities should we present them with such.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: On this note, I would like to take the opportunity to introduce a ground-up initiative developed in Bukit Panjang.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: An Emergency Preparedness Resource Team, comprising 15 young Singaporean volunteers from different backgrounds, was formed a year ago, to explore ways to build emergency preparedness capabilities in the community to prepare Singaporeans for emergencies, both in Singapore and overseas.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: The team compiled best emergency preparedness practices from both domestic and international sources.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: It also provides an Emergency Bag inventory that one may use when preparing for a disaster, a list of the various resources available in the constituency, and includes a directory of emergency hotlines in the 10 most frequently travelled overseas places by Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is my hope that this guide will help encourage greater ownership by Singaporeans in developing deeper emergency preparedness skills.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: We must ensure that both the Government and members of the public do their part to ensure our cybersecurity.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many of us are able to access information 24/7, make transactions anytime, and communicate with others through our mobile phones and social media platforms.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While Singapore's strong digital connectivity offers enormous social and business opportunities, it is also a point of vulnerability that individual hackers, criminal syndicates and state adversaries exploit to do us harm.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As Singapore moves towards becoming a "Smart City", we need to be better prepared against threats from the digital domain.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What measures does MINDEF have in place to rapidly detect and contain digital threats against Singapore?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Recent incidents of data breaches had highlighted the human factor as a major vulnerability.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, users of the Internet have long been viewed as the weak link.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: No matter how robust our Internet structure, software and hardware are, complacency, poor personal hygiene and low awareness of digital threats will endanger our SAF systems.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What steps does MINDEF have to strengthen this area and how will the Ministry ensure that internal and external audits of our digital networks are robust?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How are we getting Singaporeans to be more aware and better prepared to respond to digital threats?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Over the past year, we have seen how the spread of fake news online has divided societies, influenced elections and triggered ethnic riots overseas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, as a multicultural and diverse society, Singapore’s social fabric could easily be threatened by the spread of falsehoods that exploit potential fault lines in our society, such as race or religion.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One of the biggest challenges we face in combating fake news is on social media and messaging applications, such as Facebook and WhatsApp.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does the Ministry have any measures to counter misinformation online, such as an IT team to look into messages circulating online and intervening on the same platforms with clarifications?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: More importantly, we have to shore up our social defences, strengthening them on all fronts to counter these online threats.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: From our neighbourhoods, workplaces, markets and other common spaces, we will see and experience the real nature of our interactions and unity, making us less easy as targets.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does the Ministry have regular outreach sessions and public education initiatives to enhance our awareness of Social Defence?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can our Social Defence be further strengthened to deal with these online threats?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: It is a framework for an all-round response to threats and challenges and it involves six aspects, one of which is psychological defence.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: They also take several forms – from exploiting social fault lines in order to weaken our national unity, to eroding people’s trust in the Government.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: With the increasing use of the Internet and the social media, many of us are becoming more vulnerable to fake news and misinformation online.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: In this context, can the Minister share what MINDEF is doing to strengthen the psychological defence of Singaporeans in light of external pressures?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Joan Pereira, can you take both cuts together?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: It is, therefore, of utmost importance to instil this understanding in our youths from a young age.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: In this digital age where growing global interconnectivity may result in the potential dilution of the "Singapore Identity", it is important that MINDEF reaches out to youths to deepen their understanding of Total Defence and ensure that they remain resilient to external misinformation, misguidance and threats, especially from the digital domain.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Can MINDEF share how it is reaching out to our youths to reinforce the importance of the six pillars of Total Defence, nurture their patriotism and encourage them to play their parts for national defence?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Businesses play a crucial role in economic defence as it is critical that they are prepared for emergencies and can recover quickly from disruptions to our economy.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Therefore, it is important for the Government and businesses to work together to put in place measures to build up a strong and robust economy which would, in turn, ensure the resilience of our country.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: How is MINDEF leveraging businesses to bring across our Total Defence messages?
